generic_sampling_rules.int_primary_key: sequential unique integers starting at 1; never NULL
generic_sampling_rules.int_foreign_key: sample from parent id pool that survives PK/unique filtering; 5-30% NULL when nullable; include parent rows without children
generic_sampling_rules.int_quantity: positive integers; include boundary values and one step on each side of listed literals
generic_sampling_rules.int_general: integers within observed min/max; include min, max, and near-boundary values
generic_sampling_rules.real_measure: real numbers within observed min/max; include min, max, and one step on each side
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: short text values; include near-variants (case, whitespace, one-char edits) of listed literals
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: sample from explicit enum pool; include all listed values
generic_sampling_rules.text_date: date strings in 'D Month YYYY' format; include boundary dates one day on each side of listed literals
generic_sampling_rules.text_score: score strings like 'N–M' or 'N–M (P:Q)'; include near-variants of listed literals
generic_sampling_rules.text_nullable: non-NULL text values; 5-30% NULL when nullable
generic_sampling_rules.distinct_share: for DISTINCT-target columns, ensure duplicate share 20-50%
generic_sampling_rules.group_sizes: for GROUP-target columns, ensure group sizes of 1, 2, and >=3
generic_sampling_rules.aggregate_boundary: for HAVING COUNT targets, ensure groups with counts 1, 2, and >=3
generic_sampling_rules.comparison_boundary: for comparison targets, include exact literal, one step below, one step above, and case variants
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: for every nullable column (including nullable FKs), plant at least one NULL row and a share within the compact DB's null_share band (5-30% when the compact share is 0); never replace a planted NULL to satisfy a rule; rules and formulas constrain only non-NULL operands
generic_sampling_rules.column_length_invariant: all columns of a table must have equal length; boundary literals are placed by overwriting existing positions, never by appending
generic_sampling_rules.fk_integrity: every non-NULL FK value must exist in the parent table after PK/unique filtering; draw FK values only from surviving parent keys, and validate after insert

generation_specification.uncertainty: Total_Attendance formula holds approximately (rounding differences of up to 4); stated with condition Home_Games > 0. Home_Games observed as constant 8 (statistics distinct=1) but the rows_with_different_values target requires variation: Home_Games may vary (e.g. 1..12) to satisfy that target, and Total_Attendance must then be recomputed per row as Average_Attendance * Home_Games. Season range 2000-2030 is a loose bound from observed 2007-2013. Score shape (dash, parenthetical penalties, en dash) is uncertain / not enforced; group_sizes and aggregate_boundary on game.Score are best-effort. game.Date group_sizes and aggregate_boundary are best-effort within the 'D Month YYYY' format. Group-size and duplicate-share shaping on stadium.name and game.Date/Score must be applied in a single pass that satisfies both targets simultaneously.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: all 20 units failed with IndexError('list index out of range'); n_ok=0, n_fail=20. The traceback is not shown, but the failure is deterministic across every unit, so it is a construction bug, not a rare edge case.
issues.requested_revision: Fix the IndexError so that build_random_instance/write_instance_sqlite complete for every unit. Likely culprits to check: (a) in instance.build_random_instance, `cols = {cm.name: [samplers[(t, cm.name)].sample() for _ in range(n)] for cm in tm.columns if (t, cm.name) in samplers}` then `cols = sample_fresh_primary_keys(tm, {cm.name: cols[cm.name] for cm in tm.columns}, ...)` indexes cols[cm.name] for every column, but FK columns are only added later via cols.update(fk_cols) — so any FK column (game.stadium_id, injury_accident.game_id) is missing from cols at that point and raises KeyError/IndexError; (b) similarly `_apply_spec_rules` and the self-FK fixup loop `final = cols[pc]` assume columns exist. Reorder so FK columns are filled before PK filtering, and guard every column lookup. Re-run and confirm n_ok>0 with no errors.

issues.evidence: instance.build_random_instance: `cols = sample_fresh_primary_keys(tm, {cm.name: cols[cm.name] for cm in tm.columns}, _compact_keys(schema, t))` is executed before `cols.update(fk_cols)` is applied to the final dict? Actually fk_cols is merged into cols before this line, but the dict comprehension iterates over all tm.columns including FK columns that may not be present if fill_foreign_keys_consistently returned nothing (e.g. when parent pool empty it sets out[cm.name]=[None]*n, which is present; but if a column is neither in samplers nor in fk_cols it is absent). The deterministic IndexError across all units indicates at least one column is always missing.
issues.requested_revision: Make the column assembly total: build cols for every column of every table (sampler value, FK value, or explicit default), assert len(cols)==len(tm.columns) before PK filtering, and add a unit test that build_random_instance returns a dict with all columns for all three tables.

issues.evidence: Specification semantic rule 'stadium.Total_Attendance = Average_Attendance * Home_Games' is stated with condition Home_Games>0 and rounding ±4, supported by three rows (87047*8=696376 vs 696377 etc.). This is adequately evidenced. However the spec also lists 'Home_Games observed as constant 8 but statistics show distinct=1' while simultaneously requiring rows_with_different_values '>= 2 per group with different values' for stadium.Home_Games — these two requirements are in tension and the spec does not say how to reconcile them (vary Home_Games to satisfy the atomic op, or keep constant 8).
issues.requested_revision: Clarify the precedence: state explicitly that Home_Games may vary (e.g. 1..12) to satisfy the rows_with_different_values target, and that the Total_Attendance formula must then be recomputed per row. The program already does this in _apply_spec_rules, but the spec should say so to avoid ambiguity.

issues.evidence: Specification 'game.Season BETWEEN 2000 AND 2030' is described as a 'loose bound from observed 2007-2013' and marked uncertain; likewise 'Score format varies ... no strict formula stated'. These are flagged as uncertain in the spec's uncertainty field, which is acceptable, but the per_column_exceptions still demand group_sizes and aggregate_boundary on game.Score and game.Date without stating the value domain (e.g. allowed score shapes).
issues.requested_revision: Either promote the Season range and Score shape to firm rules with evidence, or mark them explicitly as 'uncertain / not enforced' in per_column_exceptions so the engineer knows they are best-effort. No change to program required if marked uncertain.

issues.evidence: NULL rule: spec null_targets=['injury_accident.game_id'] with 5-30% share. Program: in build_random_instance, `if key in schema.fks and not cm.notnull and cm.pk_pos == 0: share = min(0.30, max(0.05, share if share > 0 else 0.10))` — this forces a 5-30% share even when the compact DB has 0% NULLs, which is consistent with the interface rule ('at least one NULL row per nullable column'). However the same block only applies to FK columns; non-FK nullable columns (e.g. stadium.name if nullable, game.Date, injury_accident.Player/Injury/Source) get no NULL planting, and the interface rule requires NULL rows for every nullable column. Also `injury_accident.id` is a PK and correctly excluded.
issues.requested_revision: Extend NULL planting to all nullable non-PK columns (not just FKs), using the compact DB's null_share per column with a floor of at least one NULL row, and never replace a planted NULL to satisfy a rule. Verify with a post-generation check that each nullable column has NULL count >= 1 and share within the compact share band.

issues.evidence: Preservation of compact rows: writer.write_instance_sqlite copies orig_path to part and appends rows with INSERT; compact rows are never deleted or updated — good. But `con.execute('pragma foreign_keys = OFF')` disables FK enforcement during insert, so generated rows with dangling FKs (e.g. injury_accident.game_id pointing to a game id that was dropped by sample_fresh_primary_keys or drop_unique_duplicates) will be silently accepted, violating the FK integrity constraint. The spec's unmatched_join_rows target wants parent rows without children and child rows with NULL FK, not dangling non-NULL FKs.
issues.requested_revision: After inserting, run a validation pass (or enable foreign_keys=ON and use deferred checks) to confirm every non-NULL FK value exists in the parent table; drop or NULL-out rows that violate FK integrity, and report counts. Alternatively, ensure fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws only from parent values that survive PK/unique filtering (currently it draws from instance[pt][pc] before filtering, so dropped parent keys can be referenced).

issues.evidence: Reproducibility: cli._one uses rng = random.Random(seed_base*100003 + i), and build_random_instance consumes rng deterministically, so per-unit reproducibility holds. However `_init_sampler` uses `rng.choices(ov, k=min(5,len(ov)))` and `sorted({str(v) for v in literal_pool})` — the set-to-sorted is deterministic, but `rng.choices` order depends on rng state which is fine. No issue here; noted as verified.

Value variation: _apply_group_sizes reshapes values to guarantee group sizes 1,2,>=3, but it is applied to stadium.name and stadium.id and then _apply_duplicate_share is applied to stadium.name afterwards, which can destroy the group-size pattern (duplicate share reshuffles and repeats values, potentially collapsing the singleton/pair/triple structure). Similarly game.Date gets _apply_group_sizes then _apply_aggregate_boundary (which is the same function), so the second call re-shuffles and may not preserve the first pattern. This risks failing the group_sizes target.
issues.requested_revision: Apply group-size and duplicate-share shaping in a single pass that satisfies both targets simultaneously (e.g. construct groups of size 1,2,>=3 first, then add duplicates only within existing groups up to the 20-50% share), and add an assertion after shaping that group sizes 1,2,>=3 all occur and duplicate share is in [0.2,0.5].

issues.evidence: injury_accident.Player comparison_boundary: PlayerSampler includes PLAYER_BOUNDARY literals plus case variants and one-char edits, good. But _apply_spec_rules then does `vals = list(ia['Player']); for lit in PLAYER_BOUNDARY: if lit not in vals: vals.append(lit); ia['Player'] = _apply_aggregate_boundary(vals, rng)` — appending literals changes row count relative to other columns (e.g. ia['id'], ia['game_id']), so the table's columns become misaligned in length. writer uses n = len(cols[names[0]]) and indexes cols[c][i] for all columns, which will IndexError or silently truncate.
issues.requested_revision: Do not change column lengths in _apply_spec_rules. Instead, ensure boundary literals are present by overwriting existing positions (e.g. set the first k rows' Player to the boundary literals) rather than appending, and keep all columns of a table the same length. Add an assertion len(set(len(v) for v in inst[t].values()))==1 per table.

unresolved_checks: The exact source of the IndexError is not shown in the traceback; the review identifies likely causes (missing FK columns in the cols dict before PK filtering, and Player column length mismatch) but the engineer must confirm with a full traceback.

Whether the compact DB's null_share for injury_accident.game_id is within 5-30% is not shown; the program forces 5-30% regardless, which matches the interface rule but should be confirmed against the compact share.
Whether generated non-NULL FKs ever dangle after PK/unique filtering is not verified by execution (foreign_keys=OFF); a post-insert validation is requested.
Group-size and duplicate-share interaction on stadium.name and game.Date/Score is not verified by execution; an assertion is requested.

issues.evidence: Specification states 'Home_Games observed as constant 8 (statistics distinct=1)' and the Total_Attendance formula 'Total_Attendance = Average_Attendance * Home_Games' with evidence rows 1-3 all using Home_Games=8. The rows_with_different_values target on stadium.Home_Games requires variation, and the spec's uncertainty note explicitly authorizes Home_Games to vary (e.g. 1..12) with Total_Attendance recomputed. This is a self-consistent resolution, but the formula evidence is only for Home_Games=8, so the multiplicative relation for other Home_Games values is an extrapolation, not directly evidenced.
issues.requested_revision: No blocking change. Optionally note in the spec that the Total_Attendance formula is only directly evidenced at Home_Games=8 and is assumed to generalize; keep the +-4 rounding tolerance.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows many nullable columns with 'generated rows: NULL 0 / n' (e.g. stadium.name, game.Date, game.Score, injury_accident.Player, injury_accident.Source, stadium.Home_Games, etc.). Per the interface NULL rule, each nullable column should contain at least one NULL row per instance. The program only plants NULLs for nullable FKs (fk_null logic in build_random_instance) and never for other nullable columns; _apply_spec_rules overwrites values without introducing NULLs. This is a noted deviation but per instruction 7 does not block a pass.
issues.requested_revision: For completeness, plant at least one NULL in each nullable non-FK column (respecting the compact null_share band) in a future revision; not required to pass.

issues.evidence: stadium.id group_sizes target (1, 2, >=3) is nominally applied via _apply_group_sizes in _apply_spec_rules, but stadium.id is a primary key filled sequentially (range(start, start+n)) and then _apply_group_sizes reshapes it, which would create duplicate PK values. However, sample_fresh_primary_keys runs before _apply_spec_rules, so the reshaping happens after PK filtering and could reintroduce duplicates. Execution feedback reports pk_duplicates: 0 across 20 instances, so in practice the writer's INSERT ... executemany either fails those rows (counted in rows_skipped: stadium 100) or the reshaping is benign. The group_sizes target on a PK column is inherently unsatisfiable without violating uniqueness.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: drop or reinterpret the stadium.id group_sizes target (a PK cannot have group sizes >1). Engineer: remove the _apply_group_sizes call on stadium.id to avoid relying on insert-time rejection.

issues.evidence: injury_accident.id aggregate_boundary target (COUNT(injury_accident.id) with values 1,2,3) is explicitly not implemented: the code has 'if id in ia: pass' with a comment that it is best-effort and must not disturb uniqueness. Since id is a PK, group sizes >1 are impossible; the target is unsatisfiable as stated.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: remove or reinterpret the injury_accident.id aggregate_boundary target. Engineer: no code change needed given the target is unsatisfiable.

issues.evidence: game.id aggregate_boundary (COUNT(*) values 1,2,3) and game.id unmatched_join_rows are listed, but game.id is a PK filled sequentially; group sizes >1 are impossible. The unmatched_join_rows target (parent rows without children, child rows with null FK) is satisfied via injury_accident.game_id NULLs (49/253) and game rows without injury_accident children. The aggregate_boundary on game.id is not separately implemented.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: remove the unsatisfiable game.id aggregate_boundary target. Engineer: no change needed.

issues.evidence: injury_accident.game_id unmatched_join_rows lists joins_with ['game.id', 'stadium.id']. The FK is only to game.id; a join to stadium.id is not a declared FK and is not enforced. The program fills game_id from game.id pool only. This is a spec overreach rather than a program error.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: clarify that injury_accident.game_id only references game.id; the stadium.id join is a query-level join, not an FK.

issues.evidence: The spec's comparison_boundary for injury_accident.Player requires exact literal, one step below, one step above, and case variants. The program's _set_positions overwrites the first 4 positions with PLAYER_BOUNDARY (Walter Samuel, walter samuel, Thiago Motta, thiago motta), then _apply_aggregate_boundary reshapes the list, which may overwrite or reorder those boundary literals. The aggregate_boundary on Player (COUNT(DISTINCT player) values 1,2,3) is applied after the boundary placement, potentially destroying the boundary guarantee.
issues.requested_revision: Engineer: apply _apply_aggregate_boundary before _set_positions, or ensure the boundary literals survive the aggregate reshaping (e.g. reserve positions). Not blocking given execution succeeded, but the boundary guarantee is not robust.
